sheet-16-1.description: The main part of sheet 16 covers the centre of Mount Ephraim on both sides of the Black Horse Pike, which runs straight up the sheet as the dividing line between the town's western blocks and the newer subdivisions to the east. West of the Pike the blocks are laid out between Buckingham Avenue at the top, an unlabelled continuation of Kings Highway, Mt. Ephraim Avenue, Gloucester Avenue, Warrington Avenue and White Avenue, with James Street along the left edge and Bell Road running diagonally south-west from the Pike at Gloucester Avenue. East of the Pike, Kings Highway runs diagonally across long narrow lots between George Avenue, Howell Avenue and Hill Avenue, reaching the edge of Haddon Lake at the top right; New Jersey Avenue and St. Martins Avenue close the part to the south-east. Most buildings are frame dwellings with outbuildings. The commercial core around the Pike and Kings Highway has stores, a public garage, the Mt. Ephraim Hotel and the Baptist Church, and the Mt. Ephraim Public School stands on a large lot south of Bell Road. Along the Pike south of New Jersey Avenue a dash-dot line marks the boundary of the Borough of Haddon Heights, whose side streets (Wayne, Narberth and Bryn Mawr Avenues and South Park Avenue) appear only as short labelled stubs. A heavy line separates this part from the second part of the sheet in the lower right. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north rotated about 16 degrees from the top of the page.
notes: Howell (Avenue) is today the east part of East Buckingham Avenue; George Avenue is George Street; Hill Avenue is Hill Street.
Hill Avenue is drawn slanting and bent; today's Hill Street runs straight, and its junctions with Howell and Kings Highway were left out of the control (residuals of 5 to 6 m).
Kings Highway west of the Pike is drawn but not labelled on this part; today West Kings Highway.

map, 100 ft. Mount Ephraim centre, sheet 16 of the Haddon Heights series. Two parts: part 1 the main map (Black Horse Pike, Kings Highway, Buckingham, Howell (modern East Buckingham Avenue), George, Hill, Mt. Ephraim, Gloucester, New Jersey, Warrington, White Avs, Bell Rd, James); part 2 below and right of a heavy line: blocks west of sheet 21 (Spruce Av, Sartori Av, Market St, Kings Highway), drawn at the same scale and orientation but far from part 1 on the ground.

sheet-16-2.description: The second part of sheet 16, below and to the right of a heavy line, shows ground well to the west of the main part: the blocks between Spruce Avenue, Sartori Avenue, Market Street and Kings Highway, adjoining sheet 21 on the east. It is drawn at the same scale and orientation as the main part. Most of the area is a large undivided tract (lot 1A) crossed by a dash-dot borough limits line, with a row of narrow lots between Spruce and Sartori Avenues holding a few frame dwellings, a wagon shed and outbuildings. At the top right Market Street runs diagonally with a few dwellings and a store, and at the bottom Kings Highway crosses the sheet with a 10 inch water pipe; the frontage south of Kings Highway (block 109) is shown with a few buildings. The north-west side of Spruce Avenue lies outside the drawn area. Placed from two points only (a Helmert fit).
notes: Kings Highway here is today West Kings Highway.
Low confidence: placed from Sartori Avenue / Kings Highway (detected) and Market Street / Spruce Avenue (hand-picked) only.

map, 100 ft. Mount Ephraim centre, sheet 16 of the Haddon Heights series. sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 covers the northern end of Mount Ephraim (the Northmont section) between New Jersey Avenue and the Black Horse Pike, and the open land east of the Pike down to the South Branch of Newton Creek and Haddon Lake. West of the Pike the blocks are set out on numbered streets, 1st Avenue (marked not opened) at the top down through 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th and 8th Avenues, with Centre Avenue cutting diagonally across the lower left. Buildings are mostly frame dwellings, with the Northmont Hotel on 3rd Avenue, the Northmont M.E. Church at New Jersey and 6th Avenues, an auto repair shop, a public garage and a fire department house on 4th Avenue. East of the Pike a single row of dwellings lines Valley Road, which leads to a footbridge over the creek; the rest is large lots 101 and 102 with a proposed street. Township and borough lines (Haddon Township, Centre Township, Borough of Audubon) follow the creek and the lake. George Avenue appears at the bottom edge. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Centre Avenue is today Center Avenue; George Avenue is George Street.
Black Horse Pike / George Street was rejected (11.6 m off the fit).
map, 100 ft. North end: Black Horse Pike, New Jersey Av, 1st (not opened) to 8th Avs, Centre Av, Valley Rd, George Av; South Branch of Newton Creek and Haddon Lake on the east. One part.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 covers the north-west of Mount Ephraim on both sides of the Pennsylvania-Reading Seashore Lines' Grenloch branch, which crosses the sheet diagonally from the top left to the bottom centre, with Reading Avenue and Station Avenue running alongside it. East of the railroad is a regular grid of long narrow lots between Delaware, Pennsylvania and New Jersey Avenues and the numbered streets from 1st Avenue at the top to 8th Avenue at the bottom; most lots are vacant or hold single frame dwellings. West of the railroad the streets run at an angle: Idora Avenue (marked George), Lake, Charles and Lewis at the top, and Northmont, Cedar, Lambert, Hartka, Myrtle, Gaskill and Green Avenues lower down, again with scattered dwellings. The South Branch of Newton Creek and the Haddon Township and Centre Township lines run along the top. The Northmont M.E. Church appears near Centre Avenue at the lower right. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch; the grid is not drawn quite square (New Jersey Avenue diverges from Pennsylvania Avenue by about 3 degrees), which limits the fit.
notes: Idora Avenue is labelled 'Idora Av. (George)'.
Station Avenue runs beside the railroad and its junctions were left out of the control (narrow edge pairs, residuals of 4 to 8 m).
Medium-low confidence: RMSE about 5 m; the sheet's grid does not match the modern one to better than that.

map, 100 ft. North-west: Delaware, Pennsylvania, New Jersey Avs, 1st to 8th Avs, Reading Av, the P.R.R. Grenloch branch, Station Av, Northmont, Cedar, Lambert, Hartka, Gaskill, Myrtle, Idora (George), Lake, Charles, Lewis. One part.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 covers the centre-west of Mount Ephraim around Kings Highway, which crosses the sheet from left to right, and the Pennsylvania-Reading Seashore Lines' Grenloch branch, which runs diagonally down the right side past the Mt. Ephraim passenger station. South of Kings Highway a grid of narrow lots lies between Baird Avenue (5th St.), Grant Avenue (4th St.), Oak Avenue (3rd St.), Lincoln Avenue (2nd St.), Washington Avenue (1st St.) and Davis Avenue, crossed by Linwood Avenue; further south Winthrop, Garfield, Liberty and Lowell Avenues run diagonally with continuations of Grant, Baird, Lincoln and Davis. North of Kings Highway are Gaskill, Green and Hartka Avenues, Market Street (Mt. Ephraim Road), Station Avenue and Oak Avenue. East of the railroad lie Mt. Ephraim, Gloucester and Warrington Avenues, James and Bell Road, with Centre Avenue, 8th and 9th Avenues and Buckingham Avenue at the top right. Buildings are mostly frame dwellings; works include the Haddon Building Supply Co. concrete block and mill works, the Mt. Ephraim Lumber and Coal Co., and the Mt. Ephraim Fire Co. No. 1. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Kings Highway is today West Kings Highway; Oak Avenue is North Oak Avenue north of it and South Oak Avenue south of it.
Grant Avenue / Kings Highway was rejected (14 m off the fit).

map, 100 ft. Centre-west: Kings Highway, Station Av, Davis Av, Baird (5th St), Grant (4th St), Oak (3rd St), Lincoln (2nd St), Washington (1st St), Linwood, Winthrop, Garfield, Liberty, Market (Mt. Ephraim Rd), Gaskill, Green, Hartka, the railroad, Mt. Ephraim, Gloucester, Warrington Avs, Bell Rd. One part.

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 covers the south of Mount Ephraim and is turned on the page, with north to the left. The Black Horse Pike runs along the top edge as the boundary between the Borough of Haddon Heights and the Borough of Mt. Ephraim; the Haddon Heights streets meeting it (Bryn Mawr Avenue, S. Park Avenue, Prospect Ridge Boulevard, Sycamore Street, W. High Street, Maple Avenue) are only short labelled stubs. Below it James runs parallel to the Pike, with Glover and Thompson Avenues between them and a row of dwellings and a garage. The Pennsylvania-Reading Seashore Lines' Grenloch branch crosses the sheet below James. South of the railroad the land is laid out in large lots crossed by Glover and Rudderow Avenues and Bell Road, with a small grid of Liberty, Grant (4th Av.), Baird (5th Av.), Garfield, Lowell and Emerson Avenues at the lower left, mostly scattered frame dwellings. Little Timber Creek winds across the right half of the sheet, and an R.C. Cemetery and Anderson Avenue appear at the bottom right. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Line work is printed lighter than on the other sheets; detected with ink_below_paper 60.

map, 100 ft. South: Black Horse Pike (top), James St, the P.R.R. Grenloch branch, Glover, Thompson, Rudderow Avs, Bell Rd, Liberty, Grant, Baird, Garfield, Lowell, Emerson, Anderson Avs, Little Timber Creek, R.C. Cemetery. Sheet turned on the page (north to the left). One part.

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 covers the west of Mount Ephraim. Kings Highway crosses the sheet from left to right a little below the middle. North of it Market Street (Mt. Ephraim Road) runs diagonally from the top centre to the right edge, with Sartori and Remington Avenues and a proposed street running north-east across large lots, and Green, Gaskill and Northmont Avenues in the top right corner. South of Kings Highway is a regular grid of narrow lots between Adams (10th Av.), Cleveland (9th Av.), Jefferson (8th Av.), Roosevelt (7th Av.), Harding (6th Av.) and Baird (5th Av.) Avenues, crossed by Linwood Avenue, with Linden and Locust Avenues at the lower left near Little Timber Creek. Most lots are vacant or carry single frame dwellings; a garage and a few stores stand on Market Street. The top margin is labelled 'No exposure'. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Kings Highway is today West Kings Highway.

map, 100 ft. West: Kings Highway, Market St (Mt. Ephraim Rd), Sartori, Remington, Linden, Locust, Green, Gaskill, Northmont Avs, Adams (10th Av), Cleveland (9th), Jefferson (8th), Roosevelt (7th), Harding (6th), Baird (5th), Linwood Av; Little Timber Creek. One part.
